Home (Today)

Notice the iOS large-title nav with the date eyebrow, the Wallet-style stacked action cards ("6 posts ready for your review"), the "Coming up" scroller, and an Activity list written in plain sentences with no filenames. Admin gets the same page plus a Client responses card and a Compose / Batch / Upload row at the bottom — and a fifth, orange Studio tab that clients never see.

Posts — triage list

Notice the segmented control (To Review · Approved · Scheduled for clients; admin gets a fourth, Needs changes), the month pill top-right, and compact cards with a status pill, media count and comment count. Denied posts never appear on the client seat — they only show up for admin under "Needs changes". Grouped inset lists with hairline separators throughout.

Post detail

Notice that on desktop the detail opens as a 480px panel beside the list (the open row stays highlighted); on the phone it is a sheet with a grabber and centred title. Inside: a carousel with dots and a "1/3" glass counter, an Instagram-style caption with accent hashtags and "Copy caption", a message composer, and a sticky Deny / Approve footer. Approved posts swap the buttons for a green "Approved · Joust will schedule this" row. Deny always asks for a note (the field appears on tap, so it isn't in a static capture).

Assets — Library grid & viewer

Notice the 3-up (phone) / 5-up (desktop) square grid with a glass status badge bottom-left, the green ring + check on approved tiles, the To Review · Approved chips and Select button. Tapping a tile opens a full-screen dark viewer: glass top bar (close · "Library image" · "1 of 4" · status pill), a Deny · Approve · ⋯ glass toolbar, arrows on desktop. A .MOV file that Chrome can't play shows the "Preview not supported in this browser" card with Open video / Download instead of a broken player.

Collections (Tires)

Notice the collection rows — 56px thumb, "1 to review · 1 approved", a red count badge — and, once inside, the "← Tires" back button plus the pinned Reference card at the top so the client always has the approved reference image next to the new renders. Collections with nothing left for the client to see are dropped from the client's list.

Projects

Notice Open / Done sections with counts, priority dots, an "In progress" pill, and done rows struck through with green checks. The client seat is view-only — no "+" button, no tap-to-complete targets. Admin gets the "+" and the controls.

Studio Admin only

Notice the large title in Joust orange (the one admin-only surface), the Compose / Batch / Uploads / Posts segments, and on Compose the Approved Pool picker — All / Library / per-collection chips with a group label on each tile — beside a live, phone-width Preview that uses the exact same detail component the client will see. Uploads and Batch are plain drop zones with the size limits stated per endpoint.

States

Notice how the edges behave: a link without a client returns a plain 400 page with no tab bar ("This link is missing its client…"), Login follows the same tokens in light and dark, an empty month says "Nothing to review in November.", and an empty collection shows the "All caught up" check. The Home zero-state ("You're all caught up") exists in code but no sample client has zero pending items, so it isn't pictured.

How to test for real

Screenshots show the layout; three things need a live environment.

  1. Put the branch in a staging folder on GoDaddy with a copy of the database. Upload claude/portal-redesign to a sibling folder (e.g. /socialmedia-staging/) on the same GoDaddy host, import a dump of the live database into a second database, and point the staging config at that copy. Then approving, denying and uploading on staging can't touch real client data.
  2. Click these URLs on staging (prefix each with the staging folder's address):
    • /?client=kenda — Home, client seat
    • /posts?client=kenda — Posts; open one, try Approve, and try Deny without a note (it should refuse)
    • /assets?client=kenda&view=library and &view=collections — grid, viewer, Reference card
    • /projects?client=kenda — should be view-only
    • /login, then /studio?client=kenda — sign in as Joust; the orange Studio tab and "Client responses" card should appear, and /posts?client=kenda should now show "Needs changes"
  3. Check .mov playback on a real iPhone. Chrome on a Mac or PC can't play iPhone .MOV files, so every capture here shows the "Preview not supported" fallback card. Only Safari on an actual iPhone (or iPad / Mac) can confirm that the clip plays inline in the viewer and in the post sheet, autoplays muted, and that "Tap to unmute" works.

Capture artefact, not a bug: these are full-page captures. Fixed chrome — the phone's bottom tab bar and the desktop sidebar — is drawn once at its viewport position, so on long pages (Home, Posts) the tab bar appears mid-image and the desktop sidebar stops at 900px. In the real app it stays pinned to the edge of the screen.

Desktop captures are cropped to the first 1400px of page height; phone captures are complete and scroll inside their frame. All data (Kenda Tires, Klever R/T, Bearclaw HTR, the placeholder tyre renders) is seeded sample data.
